title: Cover and Move
coreMove: find the adjacent team’s exposed point and support it while preserving clear ownership of the shared mission
sourcePressure: Siloed units fail unless mutually dependent teams support one another as parts of one mission.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: teamwork means everyone helps everyone with everything
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: emergency department and radiology during a stretcher backlog
exampleSpecs.audience: an ER charge nurse whose team says imaging delays are not their problem
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients wait in hallways while each department protects its own numbers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the charge nurse sends one tech to clear transport paperwork, frees two hallway bays for returning patients, and tells radiology exactly what support they can count on
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stretcher tag dangles from a hallway rail beside a full imaging queue

exampleSpecs.domain: independent film shoot where sound and lighting are fighting over generator load
exampleSpecs.audience: a production manager trying to save the final exterior shot
exampleSpecs.stakes: the day can wrap without the critical scene if departments defend only their own setup
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the sound lead offers a lower-power recorder setup, lighting gives back one lamp, and the production manager ties both sacrifices to finishing the shot
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: humming generator dips as a rain cover snaps over the cable run.

exampleSpecs.domain: ecommerce warehouse racing a carrier cutoff
exampleSpecs.audience: a fulfillment lead watching packing blame inventory control
exampleSpecs.stakes: hundreds of paid orders miss pickup if one lane waits for the other to fail
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the fulfillment lead moves two packers to scan exception bins, inventory sends a runner to verify substitutions, and both teams protect the carrier cutoff together
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: thermal shipping label peels itself from a printer as the cutoff clock turns red.

exampleSpecs.domain: soccer team whose midfield leaves the fullback isolated
exampleSpecs.audience: a youth coach teaching team defense without shaming one player
exampleSpecs.stakes: the opponent keeps attacking the same open channel
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach freezes a drill, has the midfielder stand where the fullback needs cover, restarts play, and lets the stopped attack prove the support point
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Torn corner flag leans while the winger waits alone on the sideline.

exampleSpecs.domain: museum exhibition install where security and curators have separate opening priorities
exampleSpecs.audience: an exhibition manager balancing artifact care and visitor flow
exampleSpecs.stakes: the exhibit may open with protected objects but unsafe visitor bottlenecks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a failed walk-through, the manager pairs one guard and one curator at each fragile case, then changes the stanchion layout from both perspectives
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: glass crate sits unopened beside a coil of black stanchion rope.

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal water main repair next to a mistimed traffic signal
exampleSpecs.audience: a water crew chief and traffic technician working different trouble tickets
exampleSpecs.stakes: repair success still creates gridlock and worker danger if traffic stays unmanaged
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the water chief radios the signal tech before opening the trench, shares the lane-closure timing, and waits for the signal cycle change before moving the excavator
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: blue utility flag trembles beside a traffic cabinet with its door open?

skillTargets: identify when local optimization exposes another team
choose support that preserves clear ownership
analyze interdependence without turning it into vague collaboration

tryThisNowSpec: Name one adjacent team exposed by your team’s choices, then write the smallest support action that protects the shared result without taking over.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
